IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.2022 OF 2025  (Arising out of S.L.P.(Criminal) No.9404 of 2018)
 RAJENDRA & ORS. ... APP  VS.
 THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA & ANR. ... RES  AND  MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION NO.676 OF 2025  (APPLICATION FOR INTERVENTION)
O R D E R MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION NO.676 OF 2025 (APPLICATION FOR INTERVENTION)
The applicant has absolutely no locus to intervene.
The application is accordingly dismissed.
SLP(Criminal)No.9404 of 2018 Leave granted.

Heard the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
As per the office report, the appellants have deposited a sum of Rs.40,18,861/- (Rupees fourty lakhs eighteen thousand eight hundred and sixty one )with the Registry on 19th March, 2025.

The appellants filed a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for quashing the First Information Report (for short, the FIR) against them for the offences under Sections 420, 407 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

By the impugned judgment,
the High Court has rejected the petition.

The learned counsel representing the first informant/complainant (second respondent), on instructions of the complainant/second respondent who is present in the Court states that if the amount deposited by the appellants is permitted to be withdrawn by the second respondent, he will Rajendra vs The State Of Maharashtra on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6037365/
1 have no objection for quashing the FIR.

sentences.text: He further states that the amount will be accepted by the second respondent in full and final settlement of his claim against the appellants.
After having perused the allegations made in the FIR, we find that there is an element of civil dispute between the parties.

Hence, the FIR can be quashed on the basis of the aforesaid statements as even the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellants has no objection if the aforesaid amount is paid over to the second respondent.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order dated 11th October, 2018 is set aside.
FIR No.146 of 2015 registered at City Police Station, Udgir, District Beed, Latur, Maharashtra and all proceedings based thereon stand quashed.

We direct the Registry of this Court to permit the second respondent-Baban to withdraw a sum of Rs.40,18,861/- (Rupees fourty lakhs eighteen thousand eight hundred and sixty one) lying deposited in this Court.
The appeal is accordingly allowed.
